interest: Japanese spying and economic moves in Macao and Timor.
overview: This file comprises three diplomatic despatches sent in April and May 1937 by American Consul Howard Donovan at the U.S. Consulate General in Hong Kong to the Secretary of State in Washington, detailing Japanese economic penetration, resource scouting, and covert intelligence operations in Portuguese Macau and Portuguese Timor. Drawing heavily on information provided by British subject and Honorary British Vice Consul F. J. Gellion, the reports document Japanese bids to obtain industrial, shipping, and land concessions in Macau, negotiations for oil rights and extensive agricultural/commercial holdings in Timor belonging to the family of the late Governor Celestino da Silva, and mining interests in Australia. The file also exposes the activities of Dr. Shinzo Wada, a Japanese dental surgeon in Macau recognized as the head of Japanese naval intelligence in South China, while analyzing political tensions within Portuguese colonial officialdom regarding British versus Japanese influence.

subfiles.about: A strictly confidential report detailing Japanese bids for commercial concessions and shipping routes in Macau, covert intelligence operations led by Dr. Shinzo Wada, and negotiations for oil and mineral concessions in Portuguese Timor and Australia.
subfiles.summary: Consul Donovan reports on Japanese efforts to obtain industrial concessions, land, and shipping routes linking Macau with Canton, Hong Kong, and Timor, which were rebuffed by the anti-Japanese colonial administration under Governor Tamagnini Barbosa. The dispatch exposes Dr. Shinzo Wada, an ostensible dental surgeon who in reality directed Japanese naval intelligence across South China. Donovan further details Wada's impending expedition with retired Portuguese police officer Delfino Ribeiro to negotiate oil rights in Timor, as well as plans to inspect Australian iron ore properties.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 518 from Consul Howard Donovan on Japanese Activities in Macau and Portuguese Timor

subfiles.about: A report providing supplementary intelligence on Japanese negotiations to purchase extensive agricultural and commercial landholdings in Portuguese Timor from the family of the late Governor Celestino da Silva.
subfiles.summary: Donovan reports Japanese buyers near a deal to buy a leading Portuguese firm in Timor for two million florins.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 523 from Consul Howard Donovan on Japanese Activities in Portuguese Timor

subfiles.about: A corrective despatch amending an erroneous geographical reference concerning regional trade routes in Despatch No. 518.
subfiles.summary: Donovan corrects despatch No. 518: trade via Singapore referred to Timor, not Macao.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 555 from Consul Howard Donovan Correcting Despatch No. 518
